intent: Make the jailed lib/tests gate actually able to fail. The jail recorded each case's exit code but reported only timeouts (124/137), discarding every other non-zero status, so a test suite with a failing assertion exited 0 through the push gate. A gate that cannot fail reports safe while checking nothing.
scope: meta/scripts/shell_coverage_jail.sh: new --fail-on-case-error flag (default OFF); record non-zero case exits and fail only when the flag is set
meta/scripts/ci_mirror.sh: pass --min 0 to the suite-running invocation
Non-goal: the coverage bar stays check_shell_coverage.sh's job, per-lib and --measure'd; this gate asks only 'did the assertions pass?'
meta/scripts/lib/shell_coverage_case_runner.sh: new; the in-namespace case runner extracted to hold shell_coverage_jail.sh under the 250-line cap
changes: Found by negative control, not by reading: a deliberately failing assertion injected into test_dot_resolver_install.sh still exited 0. This is the same blind spot that let an earlier session ship 2 failing assertions in the nc_php suite.

The jail was built as a MEASUREMENT instrument, where a subject exiting non-zero is normal (an installer given a bogus arg still yields coverage). Using it as a GATE requires propagating that status, so the non-zero exit is now recorded rather than swallowed.
Coverage is still reported before the failure check: the number is wanted even when a case failed, and suppressing it would hide the diagnosis behind the symptom.
--min 0 on both gate invocations: with no --measure, the jail measured run_all.sh itself against its default --min 100 and failed the push at 54.55% -- a number neither gate asked for.

Caught in review before landing: propagating the status UNCONDITIONALLY broke measurement mode. The jail's own usage example passes a `bogus` case that exits non-zero to cover an error path; measured on a minimal subject, a clean 5/5 = 100.00% run started exiting 1. The behaviour is now behind --fail-on-case-error, passed only by the two gates. Measurement mode -- what the 105-lib campaign runs -- is unchanged.
ci_mirror.sh captures the jail's output and prints it on the failure path only. Discarding it left a red gate reporting 'suite failed: <runner>' with no warn: or FAIL: lines to diagnose from.

The added flag pushed shell_coverage_jail.sh to 285 lines and the file-length-cap hook rejected the commit. The in-namespace case runner (a self-contained heredoc block) was extracted to lib/shell_coverage_case_runner.sh, following the existing lib/shell_coverage_jail_setup.sh split. Jail 240 lines, new lib 64. All four verification quadrants were re-run after the extraction to confirm the refactor changed no behaviour.

verification.command: shell_coverage_jail.sh --subject errsubj.sh --min 100 -- "" bogus   (measurement mode, error-path case)
verification.evidence: exit=0, errsubj.sh: 5/5 lines = 100.00%. Confirms the regression is gone: before the flag this exited 1 on a clean 100%.
exit=1, 'Error: 1 case(s) exited non-zero'. Same subject, opposite verdict -- the flag is what separates the modes.
exit=0. No false positive; a green suite passes the gate. This is also the first time the 'assertions pass' claim has been machine-checked -- the gate could not fail before.

verification.command: same, with `_t_eq "a" "b"` injected BEFORE _t_report, then restored
verification.evidence: exit=1. The negative control that proves the gate can fail. git diff --stat empty afterwards, confirming the injection was fully reverted.
only my files. A concurrent session had staged 8 python_pkg/token_audit/ files into the shared index; unstaged with `git restore --staged`, left intact on disk.
all checked files are within 250 lines (was: 285 for shell_coverage_jail.sh, +35 over).

verification.command: all four quadrants re-run AFTER the lib extraction
verification.evidence: measurement+error=0, gate+error=1, gate+clean=0, gate+broken=1 -- identical to pre-refactor. shellcheck clean on all three shell files.

risks: The two modes now differ by a flag. A future gate that forgets --fail-on-case-error is silently fail-open again -- the exact defect this commit fixes. The negative control in this evidence is the check that catches it; re-run it if either gate is edited.
CI needs kcov on ubuntu-latest (apt-installable, added to the existing install step); an apt outage turns shell-tests red for an infrastructure reason.
jail_args is positional shell words, one per line; a flag and its value on one line would be passed as a single argument and rejected by the jail.
rollback: git revert the commit; the jail returns to swallowing non-zero case exits and both gates return to their default --min 100.
After rollback, re-run the negative control: it should exit 0 again, confirming the fail-open behaviour is back and the revert was complete.
